title: Trader Joe's coupon policy: the chain issues no coupons of its own
publisher: Trader Joe's (quoted via third-party reporting; the retailer's own page was not retrieved in this pass)
offer_text: "We have low prices, every day. NO coupons. NO membership cards. NO discounts. NO glitzy promotions or couponing wars at our stores. We offer the best everyday values, every day." Separately, a Trader Joe's public relations manager (Nakia Rohde) is quoted as saying: "We do not offer Trader Joe's coupons. We stay focused on providing the best everyday values, every day. However, we do accept manufacturer's coupons for other brand's products we carry."

bay_area.note: Trader Joe's operates many stores across the nine Bay Area counties. The practical consequence for Bay Area shoppers: do not look for Trader Joe's coupons, but a manufacturer coupon for a name-brand item the store carries may be honoured at the register.

sources.title: Trader Joe's Secrets You Wish You Knew Sooner
sources.evidence: Quotes the retailer's website statement and the PR manager's email about accepting manufacturer coupons.

sources.title: Does Trader Joe's Ever Accept Coupons?
sources.evidence: Independently quotes the same PR email: 'We do not offer Trader Joe's coupons ... However, we do accept manufacturer's coupons for other brand's products we carry.'

checks: Two independent third-party reports quote the same retailer statement and the same PR email
The retailer's own page was NOT retrieved, so the wording could have changed since publication
Recorded as a policy note, never as an available coupon

flags.detail: traderjoes.com was not fetched in this pass. The policy is quoted from third-party reporting of the retailer's own statement. Verify on traderjoes.com before relying on the manufacturer-coupon acceptance detail, since store-level practice can vary.

Because Trader Joe's issues no coupons, ANY site, Facebook post or Instagram story offering Trader Joe's coupons, circulars or gift cards is not official. See the excluded list for the retailer's disowning statement.

title: 2026 Sunday newspaper coupon insert landscape (what still exists)
merchant: Save (formerly RedPlum / RetailMeNot Everyday), Unilever Super Saver, P&G, SmartSource (discontinued)
publisher: The Krazy Coupon Lady (coupon media, not an issuer)
offer_text: "Save (formerly RetailMeNot Everyday and Red Plum) and less often, Unilever Super Saver are the different inserts that come out on a regular basis, although the number of inserts issued each week varies." — "The P&G coupon insert was officially gone, but it came back in 2025." In 2023 the popular P&G coupon insert ended its distribution. Their last coupon booklet was on Jan. 1, 2023. But then it came back in 2025! — "The SmartSource insert was officially gone in June 2025." We last saw a SmartSource coupon insert in March 2025, and as of June 2025, those coupons were gone for good. — "For years, we could get a full-year preview of upcoming coupon inserts, but in 2026, we no longer have a complete list."
expiry_basis: Reporting as published; KCL states it updates the post weekly as new information arrives.

bay_area.note: Sunday paper inserts are distributed regionally, so Bay Area availability depends on the local paper. The source notes Dollar Tree often carries the Sunday newspaper for $1.25 and Walmart carries it all week for at least $2, which are the cheapest physical acquisition routes in the Bay Area.

sources.title: Sunday Coupon Insert Schedule 2026 - The Krazy Coupon Lady
sources.evidence: Insert-landscape paragraphs and the month-by-month 2026 schedule read verbatim from the page, including the SmartSource discontinuation and the statement that a complete 2026 list no longer exists.

sources.title: Free Printable Grocery Coupons: 49 Best Sites to Print Manufacturer & Store Coupons
sources.evidence: Corroborates the SmartSource shutdown and adds: 'Update: Unfortunately SmartSource has pulled the plug on printable coupons and the site itself is now a part of Checkout51.' Also documents that FreeCoupons.com, CoolSavings, PPGazette and Mambo Sprouts are no longer in business or changed direction.

checks: Two independent coupon-media sources agree that SmartSource printables and inserts are gone
Neither source is the issuer, so the insert schedule is recorded as reporting rather than as an authoritative calendar
Recorded because many coupon sites and aggregators still advertise SmartSource as a live source

flags.detail: The Krazy Coupon Lady is coupon media with affiliate and sponsored content (it discloses this on the page). It is used here only to establish which coupon channels still exist, never as the source of an offer.

The publisher itself states that for 2026 'we no longer have a complete list' and that all dates are subject to change. The list above stops at May 2026 because that is where the retrieved content ended; June–December 2026 dates were not read.

Directories of 'best coupon sites' still list SmartSource.com, FreeCoupons.com, CoolSavings, PPGazette and Mambo Sprouts as sources. Several are out of business or redirected. Any list built from those directories without checking each domain will contain dead or fraudulent sources.

title: How social media was used in this research pass (and why no offer is sourced from it)
offer_text: Method note: social platforms were searched for leads only. No offer in this dataset cites Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok or any other social platform as its source of truth.

findings.facebook_instagram: Brand coupon posts on Facebook and Instagram sit behind authentication walls and are not retrievable by an anonymous crawler, so no Facebook or Instagram post could be read and therefore none is cited. Where a brand runs a social-only offer, the only defensible citation is the brand's own website or app, which is what this dataset uses.
findings.reddit: Reddit was used strictly as a lead generator. The only substantive lead taken from it was the Costco Instant Savings book cycle dates, which are recorded in the excluded list as plausible-but-unofficial and are NOT used to date any offer. Reddit threads also surfaced the getpgoffer.com P&G/Costco rebate, which was then verified directly on the official P&G microsite and IS included.
findings.tiktok: A TikTok embed appeared in retrieved content from a coupon-media page. No TikTok content was read or cited.

sources.title: r/Costco
sources.evidence: Used to locate the getpgoffer.com rebate lead and the Instant Savings cycle dates. Both leads were then checked: getpgoffer.com was verified as official P&G and included; the cycle dates could not be verified against Costco and were excluded.

checks: Confirmed that no entry in data/entries cites a social platform as its only source
Every social-media-derived lead is either verified against an official domain or recorded in the excluded list

flags.detail: Because Facebook and Instagram cannot be crawled anonymously, genuinely social-only offers (e.g. a Bay Area restaurant's Instagram-only happy-hour code) are invisible to this dataset. Closing this gap needs either an authenticated session or a manual review workflow — both are listed in ROADMAP.md.

Social platforms are the dominant distribution channel for fake coupons and gift-card giveaways (Trader Joe's, Costco, Kroger and similar). Treating a social post as a source would import that risk directly, which is why the rule is: leads yes, citations no.
